textbookText: The root is generally non-green, underground and cylindrical part of the plant developed from the radicle of the embryo. It is negatively phototropic without nodes and internodes. The whole extent of the roots of a plant is called the root system. The development of the root system differs fundamentally in vascular plants and may be classified in two groups:

a. Tap root system: The radicle elongates to form primary or main root which grows inside the soil. It produces number of lateral roots called as secondary roots, which further bear tertiary roots and Figure: 2.8.1 Morphology of flowering plant rootlets. The primary root and its branches constitute the tap root system. Tap root system is generally found in dicot plants.

b. Fibrous root system: In monocot plants, primary root arises from radicle, does not develop further and soon is replaced by many thin roots developed from the base of stem. It is known as fibrous root system. In some plants, such as grass, sugarcane, banyan tree, roots develop from part of plant other than the radicle and are called adventitious Figure: 2.8.2 Types of root system roots.

Morphologically roots have four distinct regions – Root cap, meristematic zone, elongation region and maturation region. Root cap is terminal cap like structure. It protects tender apex of root. Just behind the root cap a region of small and thin walled cells are found known as meristematic zone. They divide repeatedly and increase cell number. The newly formed cells lose the power of cell division but undergo rapid elongation and enlargement which are responsible for the increase in length of root. This region is known as elongation region. The cells adjacent to the elongation region gradually differentiate and become mature. This is known as Biology, Grade 11 | 149
region of maturation. The epidermal cells of this region form thread like tubular structure called root hairs. These root hairs absorb water and minerals from the soil.

Functions of root: i. Roots support the aerial part of the plant and fix the plant in the soil. ii. They help in absorption of water and minerals. iii. Roots prevent soil erosion by holding it. iv. The respiratory root (pneumatophore) of mangrove helps in respiration. v. The assimilatory roots are green and prepare food for photosynthesis. v. Some roots helps in vegetative propagation. vi. The roots of certain plants are modified for storage of food.

2. THE STEM The stem is the axis of aerial part of the plant. It shows positive phototropic and negative geotropic growth. Stem arises from plumule of embryo in a germinating seed. It has nodes and internodes. Branches, leaf, flower bud, fruits and bracts are developed from nodes. The portion between two nodes is known as internode. The stem is generally green during young stage and later often become woody and dark brown. The growing apex of the stem remains covered by a number of tiny leaves which arch over it. Buds are the stem’s primary growing points which may be terminal or axillary. Terminal buds are located at the tip of the stem which help in increment of length of plant. The Figure 2.8.4 Morphology of stem axillary bud is formed at the junction between a leaf and the stem. It produces the lateral branches. There are number of minute pores on stems that allow for gas exchange called as lenticels. The stem is covered by outer protective layer known as bark.

Functions of stem: i. The main stem is usually thick, aerial and stout and keeps the plant in erect position. ii. The stem conducts water and minerals from the root to the leaf. It also transports the prepared food from the leaf to the different parts of plant body. iii. Underground modified stem helps to store the food. iv. In fleshy stem of cactus help to store the water. v. The young green stem in certain plants are modified which helps in photosynthesis. vi. Thorns, the modified form of stem help to protect the plant from grazing animals. vii. Many aerial, sub-aerial and underground stem help in vegetative propagation.

3. THE LEAF The leaf is a lateral generally flattened structure borne on the stem. The leaves develop from the nodes and have axillary buds in its axil. It is normally green in colour and its main function is photosynthesis. All the leaves of a plant are known as phyllome.
